newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mark/lira seen testing 990 during European trade.
newsitem.headline: Mark/lira seen testing 990 during European trade.

text.p: The lira is seen heading higher against the mark during European trade after news Italy would re-join the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at a central rate of 990 per mark, Singapore dealers said on Monday.
They said players had been reluctant to push the lira up too aggressively due to a lack of liquidity during the Asian session.
The lira was quoted at 993.60-994.91 at 0700 GMT compared with 999.00/999.30 in late European trade on Friday.
"I don't think people have really tried to do much out here because they know the prices are going to be so wide so they've simply sold the marks out against the dollar," said a European bank dealer.
He said the dollar looked well bid across the board and could head for 1.5200 marks on the back of the mark/lira activity, despite some selling interest around 1.5180 marks.
"I'm sure we'll at least go and test the 990 support because that's the parity level," he said, adding that the lira showed potential to strengthen towards 968-970 to the mark.

"Lira's in (the ERM) with the 15-percent band. But if you look at the normal five-percent band, then 968 is the base so we could easily go down there. But I'm sure the Bank of Italy would be in at that level," he said.
Another European bank dealer said stop-loss sales were triggered in mark/lira around the 994-995 region and the cross had traded within the 992-995 range during Asian hours.
He said the mark would be sold on any rallies against the lira because the 990 lira per mark central rate was below market expectations of 1000 lira per mark.
